contract: predict(train_smiles, train_values, test_smiles, info) -> list of len(test_smiles) floats: predicted log10 property values of the test molecules. The training split of the Biogen public ADME set (Fang et al. 2023; official split of molecularinformatics/Computational-ADME) is given as SMILES with measured log10 values, the test split as SMILES only; info = {'endpoint', 'property', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, RDKit and torch are importable; wall-clock limit 540 s. Score: mean absolute error on the official test split (log10 units; minimize); RMSE, R^2, Pearson and Spearman correlations and the MAE of the training-mean predictor are reported
notes: Official train/test files of the authors' repository at a pinned commit; the candidate runs in chem_sandbox without access to the test values. No published value on these splits could be read, so none is reproduced.
protocol_description: Locally implemented or adapted evaluator for the cited task or benchmark. Data sources, generated instances, evaluation budgets and protocol differences are specified in the candidate contract, requirements and notes; scores are not automatically comparable with published results.
name: ADME: MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio (Biogen public set)
description: Predict the MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio (log10 of B-A over A-B permeability) of 529 test compounds from 2113 training compounds measured in the same Biogen assay. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error on the authors' official test split.
benchmark: ADME: MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio (Biogen public set)
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Fang et al. (2023): prospective validation of ML models for six in vitro ADME endpoints; disclosure of the 3521-compound public set.
Official train/test CSV files of each endpoint (pinned commit), MIT licence.

limitations: The test values are public in the authors' repository; a candidate that embeds them, or hyperparameters tuned on them, overfits. Treat scores as development scores.

The split files differ slightly from the values in ADME_public_set_3521.csv (up to 0.1-0.3 log units for a few compounds), and one MDR1-MDCK test compound equals a training compound after canonicalisation; the official split files are used unchanged.
The article's own results on this split could not be read (publisher site not reachable), so no published value is reproduced.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio of drug-like molecules from their chemical structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux limits oral absorption and brain penetration; predicting it from structure helps design orally available and CNS drugs.
